text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where developers frequently merge their code changes into a shared central repository. The heart of CI is automating the entire build process. Whenever new code is pushed, a CI pipeline automatically kicks in, compiling the software and running a suite of tests. This is crucial because it catches integration issues early, before they grow into major problems. If a test fails or the build breaks, the team is notified immediately, so they can fix it right away. By catching issues early, CI saves time and frustration, ensuring that the main codebase remains stable and healthy for everyone on the team.
